title: How and When to Use the Political Cycle to Identify Advertising Effects
eligible_reason: No binary staggered treatment. The paper studies political advertising (continuous GRPs / seconds of political ads by DMA-month) as an instrument for product-category advertising. All regressions are first-stage/reduced-form OLS or IV with continuous regressors: felm(log(1+GRP) ~ PGRP | MarketCode + Month), felm(GRP_Commercial ~ GRP_Political | MarketCode + Month), ivreg2 lnsales (logtotal = pgrp) with reg_zip and month FE, post-lasso IV. Fails the binary-treatment rule; IV also excluded.
design_notes: DMA (MarketCode) x Nielsen-month x category panel from Ad-Intel, RMS sales, Polk auto sales. Two-way FE (MarketCode + Month) with continuous political-ad exposure; robustness with MarketCode + Year + Calendar_Month FE; Lasso selection of instruments; auto case study in Stata with areg/ivreg2 absorbing reg_zip and i.modate. No adoption event, no event study.

specs.exclusion_reason: continuous treatment (political GRPs); first-stage regression, not a DiD

data_files_note: README.pdf: Nielsen Ad-Intel, Nielsen RMS and Polk data are under NDA; 'we provide simulated fake datasets instead'.
software_notes: R (lfe::felm, glmnet lasso) plus Stata (areg, ivreg2) for the auto case study and post-lasso IV.
priority_note: Not eligible (continuous treatment, IV design); shipped data are simulated.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Design inferred from README.pdf, 1 Main-Master.R, Workers/Table-2.R, 1-Log-Linear-First-Stage.R, 4-First-Stage-Robustness.R and 3 Auto-Master.do.
